newsitem.title: UK: Morgan Grenfell dismisses fund manager Young.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Grenfell dismisses fund manager Young.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, part of Deutsche Bank, said on Wednesday it had dismissed Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) fund manager Peter Young.

"He was dismissed on the grounds of gross misconduct late on Tuesday," a Deutsche Morgan Grenfell spokesman told Reuters, but declined to give any further details of the dismissal. Lawyers representing Young were not immediately available for comment.
Morgan Grenfell dismisses fund manager Young =2

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell spokesman James Murray said the investigation into "suspected irregularities" at three MGAM funds was continuing. Trading in the funds was temporarily suspended two weeks ago but resumed after a 180 million pound cash injection by German banking giant, Deutsche Bank.

Young, 38, was suspended by MGAM at the time the investigation -- which is being spearheaded by British investments watchdog IMRO -- was made public. An injunction freezing his assets was later obtained by MGAM and the Royal Bank of Scotland, trustee to two of the funds.

In an interview with the Daily Mirror newspaper last week, Young was reported saying he was being made a scapegoat, that his employers did not scrutinise his work and were happy to believe his track record meant he would make money.

Deutsche has pledged its support for the trusts hit by uncertainty over the level of high-technology unquoted stocks held in them. The funds saw a rapid flight of cash as soon as they resumed trading, but this slowed once the parent bank said it would support the units for at least three months.
